title: Everyday Basics
description: High-frequency words for daily life. Start here if you are new to English vocabulary study.

words.definition: to take something from someone and give it back later
examples: Can I *borrow* your pen for a minute?
words.note: You borrow FROM someone. Someone lends something TO you.

words.definition: to give something to someone for a short time, expecting to get it back
examples: She *lent* her car to a friend.
words.note: Past form: lent. Opposite direction from borrow.

words.definition: to choose what to do after thinking about it
examples: We *decided* to stay home because of the rain.
I can't *decide* which shirt to buy.
words.note: decide TO do something. Noun: decision.

words.definition: to make something clear by giving details or reasons
examples: Can you *explain* this question to me?
words.note: explain something TO someone — not "explain me".

words.definition: to keep something in your mind, or bring it back into your mind
examples: I *remember* my first day at school.
words.note: remember TO do = a duty in the future; remember doING = a memory of the past.

words.definition: to not remember something
words.note: Forms: forget – forgot – forgotten.

words.definition: as much or as many as you need
examples: Do we have *enough* chairs for everyone?
words.note: enough + noun (enough time), but adjective + enough (old enough).

words.definition: before the usual or expected time
examples: I got up *early* to catch the bus.
words.note: Opposite: late.

words.definition: making very little noise
examples: It's a *quiet* street with few cars.
words.note: Don't confuse with quite /kwaɪt/ (= very, fairly).

words.definition: paying attention so that you don't make mistakes or get hurt
words.note: Adverb: carefully. Opposite: careless.

words.definition: full of people
examples: The train was so *crowded* that I had to stand.

words.definition: having a very good taste or smell
words.note: Delicious is already strong, so "absolutely delicious" sounds more natural than "very delicious".

words.definition: physical activity that you do to stay healthy and strong
examples: I *exercise* for thirty minutes every morning.
words.note: Also: a short task for practice (a grammar exercise).

words.definition: to ask someone to come to a party, meal or event
examples: She *invited* me to her birthday party.
words.note: invite someone TO something. Noun: invitation.

words.definition: a person who lives next to or near you
examples: Our *neighbor* has a big, friendly dog.
words.note: British spelling: neighbour.

words.definition: to make something ready, or to make yourself ready
examples: I need to *prepare* for tomorrow's test.
words.note: prepare FOR an event. Noun: preparation.

words.definition: to say that you will certainly do something
words.note: keep a promise / break a promise.

words.definition: to get something that someone gives or sends you
examples: She *received* a prize for her painting.
words.note: Spelling: rec-EI-ve (e before i after c).

words.definition: to fix something that is broken or damaged
to have or use something together with other people
examples: I *share* a room with my sister.
words.note: share something WITH someone.

words.definition: different from usual, and often better or more important
examples: Today is a *special* day — it's my birthday.

words.definition: quickly and when you do not expect it
words.note: Adjective: sudden.

words.definition: to think that something is true
words.note: believe someone = their words are true; believe IN something = it exists or is good.

words.definition: to pick one thing or person from a group
words.note: Forms: choose – chose – chosen. Noun: choice.

words.definition: to say what someone or something is like
examples: Can you *describe* the man you saw?
words.note: Noun: description.

words.definition: to move or do things quickly because there is not much time
examples: *Hurry* up! The movie starts in five minutes.
words.note: be in a hurry = need to go quickly.

words.definition: to make something better, or to become better
examples: Reading every day will *improve* your English.
words.note: Noun: improvement.

words.definition: something that is wrong or not correct
examples: I made a *mistake* on the test.
words.note: MAKE a mistake — not "do a mistake".

words.definition: the condition of the air outside, such as hot, cold, rainy or sunny
examples: What's the *weather* like in your city?
words.note: Same sound as whether (= if), but a different meaning.

words.definition: feeling that you need to rest or sleep
words.note: tired OF something = bored or annoyed with it.
